question: Calculate the wavelength of the first line of the Lyman series of hydrogen spectrum. Take $R=1.097\times10^7\text{ m}^{-1}$.

options.A: For the first Lyman line, $n_i=2$ and $n_f=1$. Thus $\dfrac1\lambda=R\left(1-\dfrac14\right)=\dfrac{3R}{4}$, so $\lambda=\dfrac4{3R}\approx1.22\times10^{-7}\text{ m}=122\text{ nm}$.
options.B: For the first Lyman line, $n_i=3$ and $n_f=2$, giving $\lambda\approx656\text{ nm}$.
options.C: For the first Lyman line, $\lambda=\dfrac1R\approx9.12\times10^{-8}\text{ m}$.
options.D: For the first Lyman line, $\lambda=\dfrac{3R}{4}\approx8.23\times10^6\text{ m}$.
